items.title: Sony Music, Warner sue Anthropic, alleging a “brazen campaign” of intellectual property theft
items.summary: This latest lawsuit is particularly broad and homes in on accusations of illegal piracy.

items.title: “We’re not doing 30 bets a year”: Vijay Pande on betting small after running $4 billion at a16z
items.summary: Vijay Pande — who left a16z's roughly $4 billion biotech practice last year to start the much smaller, AI-native VZVC — talks about why biology is finally shifting from a "discovery" science to an "engineering" one, why clinical trials are still brutally expensive, and why he thinks open, shared datasets (not walled-off ones) are what will actually let AI transform medicine.
items.author: Connie Loizos

items.title: Nvidia’s AI advantage is moving beyond the GPU
items.summary: The new generation of data center systems is increasing efficiency with smarter traffic control instead of just more processor cycles.
items.author: Russell Brandom

items.title: Neocloud Lambda secures $1B in debt to buy more chips
items.summary: Neocloud Lambda has raised $1B in private debt to buy Nvidia AI chips and lease them to Microsoft. It's the latest in a string of loans, underscoring the high cost of the AI boom.
items.author: Rebecca Bellan

items.title: An Anthropic researcher just gave us a peek at self-improving AI
items.summary: Given 10 benchmarks for specific misaligned behaviors, the automated systems were able to improve performance on every single one without degrading overall performance.

items.title: Anthropic gets its first court win over the Pentagon’s supply-chain risk label
items.summary: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration illegally labeled Anthropic a supply-chain risk, handing the AI company a victory as its second Pentagon lawsuit continues in Washington.
